newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends up with cash, then slips on AGAs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends up with cash, then slips on AGAs.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures, helped by reports of a firm physical market, ended with modest gains Wednesday in sluggish trade, then slipped on ACCESS after a slightly bearish weekly inventory report.

July gained 1.2 cents to close at $2.171 per million British thermal units, then slipped to the $2.16 area on ACCESS after the AGA data. August settled 0.7 cent higher at $2.177. Most other deferreds ended up by 0.2 to 0.8 cent.
"The AGAs were a touch higher than expected. It's neutral to slightly bearish," said one East Coast trader, noting early reports of firmer cash helped lift front months today.

AGA said Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks rose last week by 94 bcf, at the high end of expectations, and were now 227 bcf, or 20 percent above year-ago levels. Eastern storage gained 63 bcf and remained 101 bcf, or 17 percent, above last year. Consuming region west inventories, which climbed by 12 bcf last week, continued to lag 1996 levels by 10 percent.

While some forecasts next week were looking for warmer temperatures in eastern and southern states, a factor that could support the market heading into bidweek later in the week, few expected a significant rally without a broad sustained heat wave.
Technically, traders still pegged July resistance at $2.21, $2.25 and $2.37. Support remained at $2.055 and $2.

In the cash, Louisiana Gulf Coast gas firmed Wednesday by two to three cents to about the $2.20 area. Midcon pipes were talked up slightly at about $2.05. New York city gate gas was quoted about two cents higher in the mid-$2.40s.
The NYMEX 12-month Henry Hub strip gained 0.6 cent to $2.242. NYMEX said 21,917 contracts traded, down slightly from Tuesday's revised tally of 22,854.

On the KCBT, July finished unchanged at $2.02, while deferreds ended narrowly mixed. The East/West spread widened by 1.2 cents to 15.1 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 155 lots traded, down from Tuesday's total of 227.
